items.explanation: や is 'ya', like the 'ya' in 'yacht'. In modern Japanese this row has only three kana.
items.mnemonic: The curved stroke and the short line are the horns of a yak.
items.culture_note: や comes from a cursive form of the kanji 也.

items.explanation: ゆ is 'yu', like the English word 'you' but short.
items.mnemonic: The big loop with a line through it is a U-turn arrow: 'yu-turn'.
items.culture_note: ゆ comes from a cursive form of the kanji 由. ゆ is also written on the curtains at the entrance of public baths and hot springs, because ゆ (湯) means hot water.

items.explanation: よ is 'yo', like 'yo' in 'yo-yo' but pure.
items.mnemonic: A yo-yo hanging from a finger: the short crossbar is the finger, the loop is the yo-yo.
items.culture_note: よ comes from a cursive form of the kanji 与.
